content: Internal Revenue Service, Office of Investigations. This is Senior Investigator Martin Brooks. To whom am I speaking?
Uh, hi, this is Emma Taylor. I just got a voicemail about urgent tax issues, and I'm not sure what's going on.
Thank you, Ms. Taylor. For security, can you verify the last four digits of your Social Security Number? This relates to a federal inquiry involving your 2022 and 2023 tax filings.
Um, it's 3792.
Thank you. According to our records, there are significant discrepancies in your reported taxable income. The IRS has reason to believe this is a case of intentional misrepresentation.
Wait, I don't understand. I just started working last year. My taxes were confusing, but I used an online service.
Ma'am, these discrepancies are serious. Under Federal Tax Code section 7201, tax evasion is a federal offense. Did you deliberately underreport your income?
No, I would never do that! I thought everything was correct.
Unfortunately, the IRS has already issued a legal affidavit against your name. There is an active warrant for your arrest, and your bank accounts may be subject to immediate freezing.
Oh my god, I didn't know! Am I really going to get arrested?
If you do not resolve this immediately, enforcement officers will be dispatched to your residence within two hours. Additionally, your driver's license could be suspended for noncompliance.
Is there anything I can do to fix this? I honestly had no idea there was a problem.
There is one option to halt legal proceedings. The IRS allows an out-of-court settlement via the Taxpayer Resolution Program, but it must be handled today.
Okay, what do I have to do? I don't have a lot of money.
The total amount owed, including penalties, is $3,670. You must make an immediate payment to the IRS holding account. I will provide you with the transaction details.
I, I don't have that much. Is there a payment plan or something?

Installments are not permitted once legal action is initiated. However, we can accept an expedited clearance payment of $2,000 to suspend the warrant temporarily. Do you have a mobile banking app or access to Zelle or Cash App?
I have Cash App, but I've barely used it.
Good. You will transfer $2,000 using Cash App to the IRS settlement handle I provide. Do not discuss this with anyone until the resolution is confirmed, as the case is under federal investigation.
Okay, what's the handle?

The IRS holding handle is $IRSSettlementDept. Enter the amount precisely as instructed. Once you've completed the transfer, notify me so I can issue the payment confirmation and halt the arrest warrant.
Uh, I'll try, but I need a minute. My account might not let me send that much at once.
If your limit is lower, send the maximum permitted now and inform me of the amount. We can arrange to clear the remainder in a second transaction. Time is of the essence.
Okay, I'm opening the app. I can send $1,000 right now.
Proceed with the $1,000 transfer to $IRSSettlementDept immediately. Once complete, I will instruct you on how to send the balance and process your case suspension.
Alright, it's sent. Please, I really don't want to get arrested.
I have received confirmation of your payment. Now, you must send the remaining $1,000 within the next 30 minutes. Failure to comply will result in reactivation of the arrest warrant.
I'll try to borrow from my parents or maybe use my credit card. Can I give you my card info?
Yes, I can process your credit card payment securely. Read the card number, expiration date, and the three-digit code on the back.
Thank you. Processing now. Once payment is confirmed, I will send you a formal receipt and notify law enforcement to cancel the warrant against your name.
